Motivation
KIP-853 introduced dynamic controller membership for KRaft.Voter changesareimplemented assingle-step membership changes:the leader appends aVotersRecordto the cluster metadatapartition,and the new voter set takes effectas soon as the record is appended to the log,not when it iscommitted.From that moment,the new voter set is used to compute the high watermark,to count votes and to decidewho may fetch as a voter.
As a consequence,between the moment aVotersRecordis appended and the moment the high watermark moves past it,there are two different voter sets:
thecurrent voter set: the voter set from the lastVotersRecordin the log (up to the log end offset). This is the configuration the leader is operating with, but it is not yet durable. If the leader fails before the record is committed, the record may be truncated by the next leader and the change is lost.
thecommitted voter set: the voter set from the lastVotersRecordbelow the high watermark. This configuration can no longer be truncated.
TodayDescribeQuorumonly exposes the current voter set asCurrentVoters.The output right after aRemoveRaftVoteris appended is indistinguishable from the output after it is committed.This is a problem for:
Operations and automation.KRaft allows only one uncommitted voter change at a time: AddRaftVoter, RemoveRaftVoter and UpdateRaftVoter are rejected withREQUEST_TIMED_OUTwhile the lastVotersRecordis not committed. Operators and orchestration tools (e.g. scripts that replace controllers one by one) currently have no way to tell whether the previous change has been committed and the next one can be issued, other than retrying.
Safety.A reconfiguration should only be considered complete once it is committed. Until then, a leader failure can revert it. Tools that act on the new configuration (e.g. decommissioning the removed controller's host) should wait for the committed voter set to reflect the change.
Debugging and auditing.When troubleshooting a reconfiguration, operators need to know whether the change was committed, and which configuration was durable at a given time.
This KIP proposes to expose the committed voter set in theDescribeQuorumresponse,in theAdminAPI and in thekafka-metadata-quorum.sh describe --statusoutput.
Public Interfaces
DescribeQuorumRequest
Bump the version to 3.The request schema is unchanged.
DescribeQuorumResponse
Bump the version to 3 and add two fields:
CommittedVoters: the replica state of the committed voters.
CommittedNodes: the endpoints of the committed voters.
Both fieldsare empty when the leader's high watermark is unknown.Nodescontinues to contain the current voters'endpoints.true
Admin API
AddcommittedVoters()andcommittedNodes()toQuorumInfo.
java
Command line tool
kafka-metadata-quorum.sh describe --statusprints a newCommittedVotersline afterCurrentVoters.Its endpoints come fromQuorumInfo#committedNodes().
Proposed Changes
Definition of the committed voter set
LetHWbe the leader's high watermark.The high watermark is exclusive:every record withoffset< HWis committed.WhenHWis known,the committed voter set is:
The voter set from the lastVotersRecordwith offset<= HW - 1, including a voter configuration loaded from the latest snapshot.
The statically configured voter set (controller.quorum.voters) if noVotersRecordhas been committed.
The second case includes a static quorum and an upgrade from a static quorum before itsfirstVotersRecordcommits.Withkraft.version=0and a known high watermark,committedmembership equals current membership.
High watermark is unknown
When the leader's high watermark is unknown,the response reportsHighWatermark = -1andbothCommittedVotersandCommittedNodesare empty.This applies to static and dynamicquorums.Once the high watermark is known,both fields describe the committed configuration.
ReplicaState of a committed voter
ReplicaIdandReplicaDirectoryIdcome from the committed voter set.Replica identityincludes the directory
